title: RFC005 §44.3 S2 RunAttempt Manifest
$comment: Closed envelope for one execution attempt of an S2 run. §44.3: every execution start creates an immutable/append-only RunAttemptManifest; an attempt that starts as `running` is finalized to exactly one terminal state (completed | failed | cancelled) by a NEW manifest document — the running one is never edited, because a crash between the edit and the write would leave a manifest that claims `running` forever. `exposure_ledger_root_hash` and `exposure_record_count` snapshot the ledger AT THAT MOMENT: the ledger itself is the durable, append-only authority (§44.2) and the manifest only references it. A completed checkpoint may only ever reference a snapshot — it can never delete earlier exposure (§44.3 last sentence).

attempt_id.$comment: make_id("attempt", "rfc005.s2-run-attempt-id/v1", {run_id, attempt_index}) — derived, never assigned, so two attempts of one run can never be confused.

attempt_index.$comment: The run's ordinal for this execution start: 0 for the first, N+1 for the N+1th. Re-running a crashed attempt takes the next index; it never reuses a burned one.

execution_profile_hash.$comment: domain_hash("rfc005.s2-execution-profile/v1", profile) over the closed {name: string} profile the attempt ran under (device, precision, batch shape, …). §44.3's 'execution_profile semantic hash'.

start_integrity_record.$comment: {name: sha256} of the inputs as they were at attempt start — the DEC-023 'nadviazať sa nesmie na výstup s inou identitou' check: a resume must re-verify this record before it may continue.

end_integrity_record.$comment: Null while `running`; a {name: sha256} object in every terminal state — even `failed` and `cancelled`, whose end record says what the attempt left on disk.
